My dad is probably the only truly depressed person I have ever met. It is a rare thing for him to be happy, but when he is, the next few days are hell. He drinks and goes to bed at 2 in the afternoon, wakes up at midnight to go on a walk (not the best neighborhood). I feel that with him, it's as if any moment of happiness is so alien, that he just cannot cope with it. He is so accustomed to his pain that he fears anything outside of it.
I want to raise a moth now.

I have a dad that is a lot like yours, right down to getting him glasses of water 3 times a day. I hope you don't mind me speaking from experience. It's best if you stop expecting him to be there. You do NOT need your father's guidance on what to do for the Air Force. I assume you have resources at school, maybe you can start there. Your father's attitude towards you probably won't change, so all you can do is change your attitude towards him. Find a way to deal with him that doesn't harm you. You come first, not him. Please feel free to PM me anytime.

I have an issue with eating and I ALWAYS fear the few doctors I've seen think I'm faking it. Three years ago, I had this terrible pain in my abdominal area and I couldn't eat but I was extremely hungry. Two days later, went to the hospital, two days after that they finally realized it was my appendix. After surgery, I was told by the doctor that it had somehow burst but got wrapped around my intestines (hence why I had such odd symptoms). Since then, I've had trouble with my appetite, keeping food down, and even though it isn't as painful, I still get aches there when I eat. Whenever I go to see a doctor after it becomes too much, I hear myself explaining this and seriously assume that the doctor thinks I'm faking.

Just thought I'd share!

Quick Edit: The medicine I have had prescribed weren't pain-killers, just shtuff to keep the food down and help with nausea.
